items.title: 52031_Kenny Clarke oral history interview
items.q: So Joe Newman's wife [Rigmor] was running the place for Joe.

ctx.x: You see? Now, then, they told me, he says, "That's all right. You'll never work in New York again." So I began to calculate, I said, "Oh, yeah, I guess I'm washed up there." It's still going on today. Because George Wein, I knew him when he was in school, in high school, because his brother -- I worked at a club, his brother was manager, at the [Kitten] Club in Boston, and George, he was about 15 or 16 years old, was still going to high school. But the message got out about Kenny is a troublemaker. So Norman…

at the Showcase and come to New York. So Joe Newman's wife [Rigmor] was running the place for Joe. [Storyville] So you know what they offered me? $50.00 a night. I said no. She said, "Well, everybody gets $50.00 a night." So then was when I learned that it was George Wein owned the place. The Storyville, or whatever it is. $50.00. That's what they offered Kenny, $50.00. She said, "Well, everybody gets $50.00." I said, "Not me." I said, "I wouldn't go around the corner for $50.00, and I've been in Paris 20 years…
Well, whatever -- I mean you're so right. Anything they do, it's done just that way.
